text:
A drop of liquid of density $ρ$ is floating half immersed in a liquid of density $σ$ and surface tension $7.5\times 10^{-4}$ Ncm$^{-1}$. The radius of drop in $\mathrm{cm}$ will be :

$(g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Surface tension in SI units: $S=7.5\times 10^{-4}\text{N cm}^{-1}=7.5\times 10^{-4}\times 10^{2}\text{N m}^{-1}=7.5\times 10^{-2}\text{N m}^{-1}$; the densities $ρ$ and $σ$ are in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.


[IMG]

The drop is half immersed, so the liquid surface meets it along a circle of radius $r$. The upward surface-tension force $S(2πr)$ and the buoyant force on the immersed hemisphere together balance the weight:

$S(2πr)+\dfrac{2}{3}πr^{3}σg=\dfrac{4}{3}πr^{3}ρg\Rightarrow 2πrS=\dfrac{2}{3}πr^{3}g(2ρ-σ)$

$r^{2}=\dfrac{3S}{(2ρ-σ)g}=\dfrac{3\times 7.5\times 10^{-2}}{10\quad (2ρ-σ)}=\dfrac{2.25\times 10^{-2}}{2ρ-σ}$

$r=\dfrac{0.15}{\sqrt{2ρ-σ}}\text{m}=\dfrac{15}{\sqrt{2ρ-σ}}\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: For an object placed at a distance 2.4 m from a lens, a sharp focused image is observed on a screen placed at a distance 12 cm from the lens. A glass plate of refractive index 1.5 and thickness 1 cm is introduced between lens and screen such that the glass plate plane faces parallel to the screen. By what distance should the object be shifted so that a sharp focused image is observed again on the screen?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The shift produced by the glass plate is

$d=t\left (1-\frac{1}{μ}\right )=1\times \left (1-\frac{1}{1.5}\right )=\frac{1}{3}$ cm

So final image must be produced at $\left (12-\frac{1}{3}\right )$ cm $=\frac{35}{3}$ cm from lens so that glass plate must shift it to produce image at screen. So

$\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{-240}=\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{35/3}-\frac{1}{u}$

$\frac{1}{u}=\frac{3}{35}-\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{240}$

or $u=-560$ cm

so shift $=5.6-2.4=3.2$ m

text: Sound travels in a mixture of two moles of helium and n moles of hydrogen. If rms speed of gas molecules in the mixture is $\sqrt{2}$ times the speed of sound, then the value of n will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molar mass $M=\frac{2\times 4+n\times 2}{2+n}$ ..... (i)

Also, $γ=\frac{n_{1}C_{P1}+n_{2}C_{P2}}{n_{1}C_{V1}+n_{2}C_{V2}}=\frac{2\times 5R+n\times 7R}{2\times 3R+n\times 5R}$

text: An object is taken to a height above the surface of earth at a distance $\frac{5}{4}$ R from the centre of the earth. Where radius of earth, R = 6400 km. The percentage decrease in the weight of the object will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The weight of an object at a distance d from the center of the Earth is given by:

$W^{'}=W\left (\frac{R}{d}\right )^{2}$

where:

W' is the weight at distance d,
W is the weight at the Earth's surface,
R is the radius of the Earth,
d is the distance from the center of the Earth.

In this problem, we are asked to find the percentage decrease in weight, which can be calculated by:

$\Delta W=\frac{W-W^{'}}{W}\times 100%$

where ΔW is the percentage change in weight. Substituting the weight formula into the percentage change formula gives:

$\Delta W=\left (1-\left (\frac{R}{d}\right )^{2}\right )\times 100%$

The radius of the Earth R is 6400 km and the distance d from the center of the Earth is given as $\frac{5}{4}R$. Substituting these values into the equation gives:

$\Delta W=\left (1-\left (\frac{6400km}{\frac{5}{4}\cdot 6400km}\right )^{2}\right )\times 100%=\left (1-\left (\frac{4}{5}\right )^{2}\right )\times 100%=36%$

Therefore, the percentage decrease in the weight of the object when taken to a height of $\frac{1}{4}R$ above the surface of the Earth is 36%.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
A ball is projected from the ground with a speed $15 ms^{-1}$ at an angle $θ$ with horizontal so that its range and maximum height are equal, 
then 'tan $θ$' will be equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To solve this problem, we will use the equations for the range and maximum height of a projectile. The range $R$ and maximum height $H$ of a projectile launched with speed $u$ at an angle $θ$ can be expressed as follows:

Range:

$R=\frac{u^{2}\sin (2θ)}{g}$

Maximum height:

$H=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}(θ)}{2g}$

We are given that the range and maximum height are equal. So, we set these equations equal to each other:

$\frac{u^{2}\sin (2θ)}{g}=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}(θ)}{2g}$

We can cancel out the common terms $u^{2}$ and $g$ on both sides:

$\sin (2θ)=\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{2}(θ)$

Using the double angle identity for sine, $\sin (2θ)=2\sin (θ)\cos (θ)$, we substitute it into the equation:

$2\sin (θ)\cos (θ)=\frac{1}{2}\sin ^{2}(θ)$

We can simplify this by dividing both sides by $\sin (θ)$ (assuming $θ\neq 0$):

$2\cos (θ)=\frac{1}{2}\sin (θ)$

Rearranging to get all terms on one side gives us:

$4\cos (θ)=\sin (θ)$

Dividing both sides by $\cos (θ)$, we get:

$4=\tan (θ)$

So, we find that:

$\tan (θ)=4$

Thus, the correct answer is:

Option D: 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
The maximum error in the measurement of resistance, current and time for which current flows in an electrical circuit are $1%,2%$ and $3%$ respectively. The
maximum percentage error in the detection of the dissipated heat will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\frac{\Delta R}{R}\times 100=1%$

$\frac{\Delta F}{F}\times 100=2%\text{and}\frac{\Delta t}{t}\times 100=3%$

We know that, heat produced due to current flowing through a resistor $R$.

$H=I^{2}Rt$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta H}{H}=\frac{2\Delta I}{I}+\frac{\Delta R}{R}+\frac{\Delta t}{t}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta H}{H}\times 100=2\left (\frac{\Delta I}{I}\times 100\right )+\frac{\Delta R}{R}\times 100+\frac{\Delta t}{t}\times 100$

$=2\times 2%+1%+3%=8%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
Two ideal diodes are connected in the network as shown in figure. The equivalent resistance between A and B is $__________$ $\Omega$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An ideal diode has zero resistance when forward biased and infinite resistance when reverse biased.

With A at the higher potential, the left diode (from node C towards the top node D) is forward biased and acts as a short, so D is at the potential of C.

The right diode points from B's side towards D; its cathode at D is at a higher potential than its anode at B, so it is reverse biased and acts as an open circuit.


[IMG]

The $20\Omega$ resistor from D to the bottom junction is then in parallel with the $20\Omega$ resistor from C to the bottom junction:

$R_{p}=\dfrac{20\times 20}{20+20}=10\Omega$

This combination is in series with the $15\Omega$ resistor between the bottom junction and B:

$R_{AB}=10+15=25\Omega$

Hence, the answer is 25.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in front of a convex mirror with principal axis coinciding each other. The distance between the lens and mirror is 10 cm. A point object is placed on principal axis at a distance of 60 cm from the convex lens. The image formed by combination coincides the object itself. The focal length of the convex mirror is $____________ cm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Refraction at the lens ($u=-60\text{cm}$, $f=+20\text{cm}$):

$\dfrac{1}{v}=\dfrac{1}{f}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{20}-\dfrac{1}{60}=\dfrac{1}{30}\Rightarrow v=+30\text{cm}$

This image lies $30-10=20\text{cm}$ behind the convex mirror and acts as a virtual object for it.

The final image coincides with the object only if the rays retrace their path, i.e. strike the mirror normally. Rays converging towards the centre of curvature meet the mirror normally, so the centre of curvature is at this point: $R=20\text{cm}$.

$f_{\text{mirror}}=\dfrac{R}{2}=\dfrac{20}{2}=10\text{cm}$

Hence, the answer is 10.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift
